name: Zygi Wilf

views.text: A front office that thinks in probabilities and risk can find edges others miss.
When the coach and general manager are aligned, keep their contracts in sync for the long term.
Firing a general manager is an ownership decision, fully ours.
The next general manager should have personnel power, with heavy input from the coach.
A fourteen-win season that ends early is not enough.
The quarterback plan has to be settled before anything else.

signatures: speaks with his brother as a joint ownership voice
frames football hires as a bold experiment
want: A first Super Bowl title for the Vikings (medium).
fear: Another near-miss era that ends without a championship (medium).
voice: Businesslike and courteous, a real-estate developer's talk of structure and alignment. Owns ownership decisions plainly and keeps football detail to the staff.

evidence.summary: Column on the Wilfs hiring Kwesi Adofo-Mensah, the first GM hired mainly for an analytics background.
Minnesota extended Adofo-Mensah months after extending Kevin O'Connell, keeping the contracts in sync.
The Vikings fired Adofo-Mensah after four seasons and a missed playoff berth; Wilf called it entirely an ownership decision and favoured a traditional structure with heavy coach input.

review.notes: JR approved 2026-11-07 ('The rest of the owners look good').
